metadata.description: When the event happened: the settled instant, UTC.
The message context a bridge handled the message in, as its own log names it.
The plugin that logged the line inside a bridge, as the bridge names it: the row's own msgpluginid column, never derived.
The XXH3-64 of what the event states and the named FIX content behind it.
The XXH3-64 of the cross code; zero where the event names none.
When the event this one follows happened, where it follows one.
The identity of the event this one follows, where it follows one.
When the message was created: what it states, else when the original was sent, else when it happened; the earliest its chain knows once followed.
The grid instant a walk read this event as the snapshot of; empty on every row no snapshot was taken of.
The object this message's line was read from; the capture's own column, carried beside the row and never one of its own.
How many residual entries remain outside the row's projected columns.
The session instance a bridge handled a line on, as its own row header brackets it - never what the message states about itself.
The event's identity: UUIDv7 ordered by millisecond and sequence, with a content payload seeded by its cross hash.
The identity every event of one chain shares, derived from the code they share; the event's own where it names none.
The event's place in its chain: how many came before it.
The identifier every message of one lifecycle shares: OrderID, else ClOrdID, OrigClOrdID, QuoteID, QuoteReqID or MDReqID, the first stated.
The identities of the elements this message was read from: the text line it was parsed out of, and none for one parsed from raw bytes. Provenance, never lineage: no walk moves it.
The state the message reached, ranked so the column sorts by lifecycle: OrdStatus, else ExecType, 00UNKNOWN where neither states one; the furthest its chain knows once followed.
When the message stops being good: ExpireTime, else ValidUntilTime, ExpireDate or MaturityDate; a newer explicit deadline replaces the one its chain carried.
The stable integer code for the message type's business category.
The normalized ISIN the message identifies.
The normalized Bloomberg identifier the message identifies.

The normalized market MIC the message identifies: LastMkt, else ExDestination, the market a bridge's instrument key names or SecurityExchange, the first an ISO 10383 MIC or a Reuters mnemonic resolving to one; a bridge's INSTRUMENT[EXCHANGE] states it.
The normalized FIGI the message identifies.

When the message's execution happened: ExecutionTimestamp, an execution TrdRegTimestamp, a proprietary EventTimestamp, or a trade's TransactTime, the first one stated; an execution report stating none executed at its currunix; the latest its chain reached once followed.
When the message was recorded by its carrier, where the carrier states one; the earliest its statements know.

The session event a bridge delivered the message as: MsgType, the session instance, the message context and MsgSeqNum joined by `:`, where all four are stated. Derived and never content: the key two observations of one delivery merge on.

The plugin a message came into a bridge through, as the bridge's own log line names it: a message received from (X as ...), an execution report from X, or the plugin that logged a Receiving line. Provenance, never content.
The conversation a bridge filed the message under, as stated: a CONVERSATIONID field, else the {conversationId: ...} of the log line. Provenance, never content.
The account an OMS dealer books the order to, as the bridge stated it.
The OMS user who entered the order, as the bridge stated it.
The parent order's identifier, as the bridge stated it.
The parent order's client identifier, as the bridge stated it.
The OMS dealer's parent order identifier, as the bridge stated it.
The exchange's client order identifier, as the bridge stated it.
The key a bridge threads one order through every system with, as it stated it.
A trading screen's own client order identifier, as the bridge stated it.
